message.content:
**Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of May 2026)** | Area | What You’re Generally Entitled To | |------|-----------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent.
• Must return deposit within 30 days after you move out unless deductions are made for damages beyond normal wear and tear. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlords must keep premises safe, sanitary, and fit for habitation—plumbing, heating/cooling, structural integrity, pest control, etc.
• If repairs aren’t done promptly, you can request them in writing; if ignored, you may have grounds to reduce rent or terminate the lease. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due when specified in your lease (often monthly).
• Late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease and cannot exceed $50 per day. | | **Lease Termination / Move‑Out Notice** | • For month‑to‑month leases, either party needs at least 30 days’ written notice before ending tenancy.
• For fixed‑term leases, you generally owe rent until the end of the term unless there’s a breach by landlord. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord must respect your right to live peacefully; they can’t enter except under limited circumstances (emergency, repair, inspection) and usually must give reasonable notice (at least 24 hours). | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, marital status, source of income, or other protected classes. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve proper eviction notices (e.g., “Notice to Pay Rent” or “Notice to Cure”) and follow court procedures. Unlawful evictions (“self‑eviction,” “no‑notice” evictions) violate both state and federal laws. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct Option** *(limited)* | • In some cases, tenants may fix minor issues themselves and deduct costs from rent—but this is rarely permitted in Texas residential rentals and typically requires prior agreement. | ### Quick Tips 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully:** It often contains specifics that override generic rules (like extra security deposits or pet restrictions). 2. **Document Everything:** Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of damage, and maintenance requests. 3. **Know When to Seek Legal Help:** If disputes arise over deposits, habitability, or unlawful eviction attempts, consider contacting a local attorney or the Texas Attorney General’s Office. These points cover most common scenarios, but individual situations can vary. Always check the latest statutes or consult a qualified professional if you face a unique issue.
